messages:
maria.k: heads-up — brought up a new cross-encoder candidate quantized to int8 and saw a drop in ranking metrics on webqa.
samuel_r: can you paste the eval command + seed? could be eval-config mismatch rather than model quality.
maria.k: sure: `python eval/runner.py --model hf/crossenc-small-v2 --quant int8 --dataset webqa-release-v2 --qfmt 'query: {q}\nctx: {d}' --tokenizer roberta --seed 42` -> NDCG@10 0.372 vs fp16 0.384. didn't touch truncation flags.
lee_eng: did you use the pipeline change we rolled last week (doc concat_left vs concat_right)? ordering can move relevant terms across context boundary and affect NDCG/MRR.
maria.k: oh good point — I used `concat_left`. quick re-run with `concat_right` gives NDCG@10 0.383. so ordering explains most of the gap.
nora_pm: quick Q — which slice of webqa? full set or head/tail? important for product impact.
maria.k: full webqa-release-v2 (~3k queries) and a small head/tail split. the full diff is dominated by ~10% tail queries where short queries hit different token boundaries.
eval-bot: eval-bot: job 89421 completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/89421/metrics.json. summary: NDCG@10 int8=0.372, fp16=0.384, delta=-3.12%, paired t-test p=0.02.
samuel_r: p=0.02 is worth looking at but run paired bootstrap for CI. also try forcing canonical query formatting to rule out punctuation/tokenization noise.
maria.k: did bootstrap(10k): int8 mean=0.372 ±0.006, fp16 mean=0.384 ±0.004. paired bootstrap p~=0.01. reformatting test incoming.
lee_eng: another hypothesis: quantized kernels slightly change KV-cache alignment for short sequences. try canonicalizing queries (strip punctuation, normalize whitespace) and enforce doc chunking at 512 tokens.
maria.k: running canonicalization ablation now: `scripts/normalize_queries.py --strip-punct --lower --max-tokens 32` + doc chunking 512. also trying mixed-precision fallback (int8 cache + fp16 attention) to see if we can recover.
nora_pm: if formatting normalization fixes it, we should bake that into our model onboarding checklist so customers don't see regressions when we swap quantized variants.
samuel_r: agree. also run the same tests across other datasets (nq-open, ty-pos) to ensure it's not dataset-specific.
maria.k: plan: 1) canonicalization ablation (today) 2) cross-dataset sanity (today) 3) mixed-precision staging run (tomorrow) 4) write a per-slice report and suggested rollout/fallback policy. will attach artifacts and a short tl;dr.
lee_eng: :thumbsup: ping me when artifacts are up so we can sketch an automated normalization step in the eval pipeline.
eval-bot: eval-bot: PR #4529 opened with artifact links and badges: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/4529. CI shows failing metric check (expected delta < 1%).
